findings.title: The readback is of the DXT5-compressed copy, so edge pixels may already be darkened before the bleed runs
findings.detail: With Prefs.TextureCompression on (the default) and the PNG's sides divisible by 4, vanilla compresses the PNG to DXT5 at load (Texture2D.Compress, or StaticTextureAtlas.FastCompressDXT with the EncodeBC3_AMD kernel). The Graphics.Blit in TextureEdgeBleed.ReadPixels reads that compressed copy, not the PNG. DXT5 shares one colour range per 4x4 block, and the black transparent pixels of a cut edge sit in the same blocks as the visible edge pixels. Unless the encoder weights colour by alpha, which I could not confirm (so this part is opinion), those edge pixels are already pulled toward black when read back, and the bleed copies that darker colour outward: the seam is reduced but may not go away. One change in ReadPixels: when the source is compressed, decode the original PNG bytes with Texture2D.LoadImage (needs the texture path passed down from MakeShieldGraphic) rather than blitting the GPU copy. That also removes the RenderTexture and colour-space round trip. Worth confirming in game with Texture Compression on and then off before changing anything.

findings.title: The temporary readable Texture2D is not destroyed if ReadPixels throws
findings.detail: In TextureEdgeBleed.ReadPixels, UnityEngine.Object.Destroy(readable) is inside the try block, after ReadPixels, Apply and GetPixels32. If any of them throws, Apply's catch logs the warning but the full-size Texture2D is never freed. FiringArc already does this the safer way: declare it null before the try and destroy it in finally. A one-time cosmetic path, so it only matters on the failure branch.

findings.title: The bled copy is uncompressed RGBA32, about 4x the memory of the DXT5 copy it replaces
findings.detail: Vanilla keeps mod PNGs as DXT5 when compression is on. The replacement is created as TextureFormat.RGBA32 with a full mip chain and never compressed. For the current ~128px shield canvases this is negligible. It grows with every future shield texture, and calling result.Compress(true) before Apply would undo it, but compressing would bring back the same block-sharing caveat as above.
